newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel closed almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies following intervention by the Bank of Israel, dealers said.

"The shekel gained against the dollar following the dollar's decline against the mark and the Bank of Israel had to intervene, buying dollars to support the basket," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The central bank intervened on a very low scale and after the setting of the representative rate the basket fell to 7.04 percent below the slope," he said.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1700 against 3.1710 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5494 shekels against 3.5495 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8778 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8781 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0973 shekels per mark against 2.0967 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1690 shekels.
